title: Eukaryotic cell ultrastructure; DNA replication
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE02b#t3 term and clue written for the game; CE02a#t1 term and clue written for the game; GE01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; CE02b#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE02a#N.8a, GE01a#N.2a, CE02a#N.11a, GE01a#N.4a, CE02a#N.12, GE01a#N.6a, GE01a#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Chitin
items.clue: The substance that fungal walls are made of

items.label: Nucleolus
items.clue: Dense region that makes rRNA and assembles ribosomes

items.label: Interphase
items.clue: Period before a cell divides, in which its DNA is copied.

items.label: Stroma
items.clue: Fluid inside a chloroplast containing the enzymes that make sugars

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes a membrane-bound organelle of a eukaryotic cell?

options.text: The Golgi apparatus is a stack of flattened sacs studded with ribosomes that synthesise proteins.
Mitochondria are bounded by a single membrane folded inward to form cristae.
Lysosomes are vesicles bounded by a single membrane that contain hydrolytic enzymes.
Secretory vesicles are lysosomes under another name, digesting worn-out organelles.

questions.explanation: Lysosomes are single-membrane sacs containing hydrolytic enzymes, kept separate from the rest of the cytoplasm, that digest material taken in and worn-out organelles.

questions.stem: A cut in the skin heals as new skin cells are produced by cell division. Why must DNA replication take place before each of these divisions?

options.text: So that the existing DNA can be divided equally, half going to each of the new cells.
So that each new cell receives a complete copy of the DNA with an identical base sequence.
It does not need to take place, because replication is only required for reproduction.
So that the original DNA can stay intact in one cell and the other cell gets a new copy.

questions.stem: In an electron micrograph of an animal cell, a structure appears as a discrete stack of curved, flattened membrane sacs with small vesicles budding from its edges and no ribosomes attached. Which structure is it?

options.text: Golgi apparatus, where proteins are modified and packaged
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum, where lipids are made
Mitochondrion, where aerobic cell respiration is carried out
Rough endoplasmic reticulum, where secreted proteins are made

questions.explanation: A stack of curved sacs, separate from the nuclear envelope, with no ribosomes and vesicles budding from its edges as proteins are packaged for transport.

questions.stem: A drug inhibits helicase but has no effect on DNA polymerase. What will happen to DNA replication in a cell treated with the drug?

options.text: Replication continues normally, because DNA polymerase unwinds the double helix itself as it copies each strand.
New strands are made but fall off the template, because helicase forms the hydrogen bonds that hold new bases in place.
Cell division continues without replication, because the existing DNA is simply shared between the two daughter cells.
Replication cannot begin, because the hydrogen bonds between the strands are not broken, so no template strand is exposed.

questions.stem: An electron micrograph of a cell shows a large amount of rough ER, a large Golgi and many small vesicles close to the cell surface. What does this cell most likely do?

options.text: It makes large amounts of lipid, using the ribosomes on its ER.
It digests engulfed bacteria, using the enzymes in its many vesicles.
It makes proteins, such as enzymes, and releases them from the cell.
It makes proteins in the Golgi, which the ER then packs into vesicles.

questions.explanation: RER makes proteins; the Golgi modifies and packages them; vesicles carry them to the surface for release.

questions.stem: During replication, a section of a template strand with the base sequence TACGGA is copied. Which statement describes the new strand built on this section?

options.text: Its sequence is TACGGA, an exact copy of the template strand it was assembled on.
Its sequence is AUGCCU, because uracil replaces thymine in each newly made strand.
Its sequence is ATGCCT, held to the template by covalent bonds made by DNA polymerase.
Its sequence is ATGCCT, the complement of the template, held to it by hydrogen bonds.

questions.explanation: A pairs with T and G with C, so the new strand reads ATGCCT and is held to the template by hydrogen bonds between paired bases.

questions.stem: A short section of a DNA molecule has one strand reading GATTC, paired base by base with a second strand reading CTAAG. The molecule is replicated once. Which statement describes the two DNA molecules produced?

options.text: Each is GATTC paired with CTAAG; each has one strand of the original molecule and one new strand.
Each is GATTC paired with CTAAG; one has both original strands and the other has two new strands.
One is GATTC paired with GATTC and the other is CTAAG paired with CTAAG.
One gets the bases GAT paired with CTA, and the other gets TC paired with AG.

questions.explanation: Each original strand was a template for a new, complementary partner. Both molecules match the parent, and each keeps one original strand: semi-conservative.
